final_candidate.name: pore_to_molecule_fit_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how tightly a molecule geometrically fits inside the framework's largest accessible free-space region, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest included free sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) is large relative to the molecule's maximum heavy-atom extension (GeDi) permit more retained rotational and translational freedom, hence smaller entropy loss; frameworks where the molecule nearly fills the free space force greater entropy loss. This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-size vs rotational-entropy-loss comparison (E02, C2) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03, C3) into a molecule-framework coupling descriptor.
final_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement coupling between adsorbate size and framework free space. lsd_p is used as the included-along-free-path sphere (Dif), NOT the passing bottleneck Df and NOT a global cavity diameter Di; the E02 'cavity diameter' mechanism is therefore only proxied, since Dif measures the largest sphere sitting along the free-sphere path rather than an average or global cavity size. GeDi is the largest distance between two heavy atoms in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full all-atom molecular envelope (hydrogens excluded) and is legitimately zero for the 54 single-site species; at GeDi = 0 the ratio degenerates to 1, which should be read as 'no resolvable size-based confinement penalty for this proxy', not as a physical claim of free rotation. The ratio is dimensionless, bounded in (0, 1], uses only native inputs and arithmetic, and requires no rotor_case branching because no inertia logs are taken. This is an empirical proxy construction; the source evidence reports qualitative comparisons on specific zeolite pairs (MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, MCM-22) and supplies no fitted coefficients, so no source-specific percentage is imported.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The descriptor fails if (1) within the training range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) at fixed GeDi, the conditional physical entropy loss does not decrease as the ratio increases (i.e., the fit-to-confinement hypothesis has the wrong sign or no signal); or (2) a competing explanation accounts better: entropy loss driven instead by framework chemistry/adsorption energetics or by the passing bottleneck lsd_f rather than the included sphere lsd_p, in which case swapping lsd_p for lsd_f in the same ratio would outperform, indicating the Dif role assignment was wrong; or (3) the signal is carried entirely by GeDi alone (molecule-size effect) with no incremental framework-dependence, reducing the ratio to a disguised adsorbate-size descriptor.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes: (a) lsd_p (Dif) is a usable proxy for the confining free-space scale relevant to retained rotational/translational freedom, acknowledging it is neither Df nor a guaranteed global cavity diameter; (b) GeDi proxies the molecule's largest spatial extension relevant to rotating inside the pore, acknowledging hydrogens are excluded and single-site species give GeDi = 0 by definition; (c) the additive denominator (lsd_p + GeDi) is a fixed monotone normalization choice, not a physical free-volume equality; (d) the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy-loss comparisons in zeolites transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime; none of these assumptions establishes causality.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom, GeDi in [0, 10.9718] angstrom. The ratio is strictly positive and bounded in (0, 1] over this support; no division-by-zero occurs because lsd_p > 0 throughout training and the denominator adds a positive constant. GeDi = 0 (54 single-site species) yields ratio = 1, a legitimate boundary value of the heavy-atom proxy, not a physical claim of unrestricted rotation; these points should be checked as a separate rotor_case branch rather than median-imputed.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

draft.name: pore_to_molecule_fit_ratio
draft.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how tightly a molecule geometrically fits inside the framework's largest accessible free-space region, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest included free sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) is large relative to the molecule's maximum heavy-atom extension (GeDi) permit more retained rotational and translational freedom, hence smaller entropy loss; frameworks where the molecule nearly fills the free space force greater entropy loss. This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-size vs rotational-entropy-loss comparison (E02, C2) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03, C3) into a molecule-framework coupling descriptor.
draft.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement coupling between adsorbate size and framework free space. lsd_p is used as the included-along-free-path sphere (Dif), NOT the passing bottleneck Df and NOT a global cavity diameter Di; the E02 'cavity diameter' mechanism is therefore only proxied, since Dif measures the largest sphere sitting along the free-sphere path rather than an average or global cavity size. GeDi is the largest distance between two heavy atoms in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full all-atom molecular envelope (hydrogens excluded) and is legitimately zero for the 54 single-site species; at GeDi = 0 the ratio degenerates to 1, which should be read as 'no resolvable size-based confinement penalty for this proxy', not as a physical claim of free rotation. The ratio is dimensionless, bounded in (0, 1], uses only native inputs and arithmetic, and requires no rotor_case branching because no inertia logs are taken. This is an empirical proxy construction; the source evidence reports qualitative comparisons on specific zeolite pairs (MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, MCM-22) and supplies no fitted coefficients, so no source-specific percentage is imported.
draft.falsification_criteria: The descriptor fails if (1) within the training range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) at fixed GeDi, the conditional physical entropy loss does not decrease as the ratio increases (i.e., the fit-to-confinement hypothesis has the wrong sign or no signal); or (2) a competing explanation accounts better: entropy loss driven instead by framework chemistry/adsorption energetics or by the passing bottleneck lsd_f rather than the included sphere lsd_p, in which case swapping lsd_p for lsd_f in the same ratio would outperform, indicating the Dif role assignment was wrong; or (3) the signal is carried entirely by GeDi alone (molecule-size effect) with no incremental framework-dependence, reducing the ratio to a disguised adsorbate-size descriptor.

review_issues.explanation: Execution check reports a rejected mapping: 'Wrong physical variable mapping: GeDi requires heavy_atom_pair_distance'. The draft's hypothesis text describes GeDi as the molecule's 'maximum heavy-atom extension' relevant to rotating inside the pore, which glosses the defined role (largest distance between two molecular atoms, heavy-atom implicit-H representation). The mismatch between the prose framing (molecular envelope/size for rotation) and the defined quantity_role (heavy_atom_pair_distance) must be recorded; the slot remains rejected pending independent review.

Proxy-role mismatch for lsd_p: E02 explicitly identifies 'the average cavity diameter' as the descriptor of confinement extent, whereas lsd_p is Zeo++ Dif, the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path — neither the global cavity diameter Di, nor the passing bottleneck Df, nor an average over the cavity. The draft acknowledges this, but the review records that the E02 cavity-diameter mechanism is only proxied, not directly instantiated, by lsd_p.

GeDi measures maximum pairwise heavy-atom separation (an elongation/extremal length), not a rotational-freedom measure such as the radius of gyration compared against available cage space in E06. The mapping from extremal length to rotational confinement is an unverified empirical choice, not a defined physical correspondence.

Degeneracy at the upper boundary: the ratio lsd_p/(lsd_p+GeDi) equals 1 both when GeDi=0 (the 54 legitimate single-site zeros of the heavy-atom proxy) and in the limit lsd_p >> GeDi. The value 1 therefore conflates 'proxy carries no size information' with 'very loose geometric fit'; the draft flags the GeDi=0 case but the conflation with the large-pore limit is a distinct ambiguity of the descriptor's interpretation.

The denominator (lsd_p + GeDi) is an ad hoc additive normalization mixing two quantities of the same unit but different physical roles (framework included-sphere diameter and adsorbate heavy-atom pair distance). It is not a physical free-volume equality, and AV/Vol-based free-volume reasoning would be invalid here; the draft states this, but the review records the normalization choice as purely empirical.

E02 and E01/E04 report specific zeolite-pair comparisons (FER vs FAU; MFI vs FAU) with unresolved temperature, loading, and framework chemistry. The hypothesis transfers these qualitative comparisons to the benchmark regime; this transfer remains a hypothesis and no source supplies fitted coefficients, so no source-specific percentage or constant may be imported.

E06 concerns MCM-22 supercage adsorption of linear and singly branched molecules, with diffusion discussed at 450–850 K; the source proposes only a possible qualitative effect of rotational freedom on adsorption equilibrium. Transfer to all benchmark frameworks and to the entropy-loss target is not established by the source.

E05 warns that treating confined guests under RRHO with retained mobility neglected overestimates entropy losses, and that mobility must be accounted for; this constrains any interpretation of the descriptor as directly measuring lost rotational/translational freedom, since the descriptor is built from static geometry only and captures no adsorbed-phase mobility information.

The conditional prediction (entropy loss decreases as lsd_p increases at fixed GeDi) is a stated hypothesis, not a verified mechanism. The descriptor is a monotone saturating function of lsd_p, so it cannot distinguish between 'confined freedom' and other monotone pore-size effects; falsification criterion (3) (signal carried entirely by GeDi) correctly identifies that the ratio may reduce to a disguised adsorbate-size descriptor, but this has not been excluded.

Knowledge-graph proxy edges (e.g., cavity_rotation→lsd_p, cavity_rotation→GeDi) are conditional MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS relations, not causal or executed checks. Absent graph edges to any descriptor are unknown support, not disproof; the descriptor's mechanism status stays unverified until independent quantitative evaluation.

No target values are provided and the target is defined as entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas−Sads)/R with the ANN predicting Sads/Sgas; the hypothesis' claimed monotone relation between the descriptor and entropy loss cannot be checked from the supplied materials and must remain unverified rather than assumed.

GeDi measures maximum pairwise heavy-atom separation (an elongation/extremal length), not a rotational-freedom measure such as the radius of gyration compared against available cage space in E06. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: If the translational component of adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how much a molecule's spatial extent is confined by the framework's narrowest accessible passage, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest passing free sphere (lsd_f, the Df bottleneck) is large relative to the molecule's heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) permit more retained translational freedom and hence smaller entropy loss, while frameworks whose bottleneck barely admits the molecule force greater translational entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03) into a bottleneck-side molecule-framework coupling descriptor, complementary to the round-1 included-sphere descriptor lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi).
descriptor_candidate.rationale: lsd_f is the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path (a bottleneck proxy), NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the included-along-path Dif used in round 1; using it assumes that confinement experienced by an adsorbate is at least partly controlled by the narrowest constrictions connecting accessible space, which is an assumption, not an established fact. SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full van der Waals extent (hydrogens excluded) and legitimately equals zero for the 54 single-site training rows; at SPAN = 0 the descriptor equals 1, which is finite and physically interpretable as no geometric confinement for a point-like adsorbate. The descriptor is dimensionless, defined for all training support (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom, SPAN in [0, 6.24083] angstrom), and requires no logs of inertia so no rotor_case branch is needed. Mechanistically it targets the translational freedom channel named in E03; it makes no claim about rotational freedom, energetics, or framework chemistry, and it does not assert that the bottleneck equals the local adsorption environment (adsorption may occur in cavities larger than the bottleneck).
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding SPAN fixed within its training quantiles, entropy loss increases rather than decreases with increasing lsd_f, or if the empirical loss is better explained by cavity-size proxies (e.g., lsd_p-based or AV-based descriptors) with no residual dependence on the bottleneck lsd_f — which would indicate confinement is set by the adsorption site volume, not the narrowest passage. descriptor_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) lsd_f (Df bottleneck) is a usable proxy for the constriction-controlled part of translational confinement, distinct from cavity Di and from Dif; (2) SPAN (heavy-atom, implicit-H) is a usable proxy for molecular spatial extent, acknowledging hydrogen atoms are excluded; (3) a saturating ratio form lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) approximates retained translational freedom, with no fitted coefficients; (4) transfer of reported MFI/FAU/FER confinement-entropy statements to the benchmark regime at unspecified temperature and loading is hypothetical. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. draft.name: bottleneck_to_molecule_span_translational_freedom_ratio
draft.hypothesis: If the translational component of adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how much a molecule's spatial extent is confined by the framework's narrowest accessible passage, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest passing free sphere (lsd_f, the Df bottleneck) is large relative to the molecule's heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) permit more retained translational freedom and hence smaller entropy loss, while frameworks whose bottleneck barely admits the molecule force greater translational entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03) into a bottleneck-side molecule-framework coupling descriptor, complementary to the round-1 included-sphere descriptor lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi).
draft.rationale: lsd_f is the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path (a bottleneck proxy), NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the included-along-path Dif used in round 1; using it assumes that confinement experienced by an adsorbate is at least partly controlled by the narrowest constrictions connecting accessible space, which is an assumption, not an established fact. SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full van der Waals extent (hydrogens excluded) and legitimately equals zero for the 54 single-site training rows; at SPAN = 0 the descriptor equals 1, which is finite and physically interpretable as no geometric confinement for a point-like adsorbate. The descriptor is dimensionless, defined for all training support (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom, SPAN in [0, 6.24083] angstrom), and requires no logs of inertia so no rotor_case branch is needed. Mechanistically it targets the translational freedom channel named in E03; it makes no claim about rotational freedom, energetics, or framework chemistry, and it does not assert that the bottleneck equals the local adsorption environment (adsorption may occur in cavities larger than the bottleneck).
draft.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding SPAN fixed within its training quantiles, entropy loss increases rather than decreases with increasing lsd_f, or if the empirical loss is better explained by cavity-size proxies (e.g., lsd_p-based or AV-based descriptors) with no residual dependence on the bottleneck lsd_f — which would indicate confinement is set by the adsorption site volume, not the narrowest passage. A competing explanation is that the descriptor merely correlates with framework density or ASA through framework topology rather than encoding a translational-confinement mechanism; this must be excluded before attributing the mechanism.
draft.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) lsd_f (Df bottleneck) is a usable proxy for the constriction-controlled part of translational confinement, distinct from cavity Di and from Dif; (2) SPAN (heavy-atom, implicit-H) is a usable proxy for molecular spatial extent, acknowledging hydrogen atoms are excluded; (3) a saturating ratio form lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) approximates retained translational freedom, with no fitted coefficients; (4) transfer of reported MFI/FAU/FER confinement-entropy statements to the benchmark regime at unspecified temperature and loading is hypothetical. No causal or novel mechanism is claimed; the descriptor is a testable geometric coupling proxy.
draft.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: lsd_f is strictly positive (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the denominator never vanishes; SPAN = 0 for 54 single-site training rows is a legitimate physical zero preserved by the expression (descriptor = 1, no division by SPAN), not imputed or excluded; descriptor range is (0, 1] and monotone decreasing in SPAN and increasing in lsd_f.

review_issues.explanation: Proxy mapping from source to descriptor is a definitional mismatch: E02 names the average cavity diameter as the confinement descriptor in the FER/FAU comparison, while the draft uses lsd_f (Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere passing through a periodic free path). Per the preserved diameter_roles constraint, Df is neither the global cavity Di nor the included-along-path Dif, and C2's transfer assumptions explicitly require that the cavity-to-lsd_f proxy mapping 'must be justified'; the draft acknowledges the distinction in its rationale but supplies no independent justification for treating the passing bottleneck as the confinement-controlling quantity. Adsorption sites are typically cavities larger than the bottleneck, so a molecule may reside in an environment geometrically unrelated to lsd_f.

Geometric quantity mismatch on the adsorbate side: SPAN is defined as a center-of-mass-centered enclosing radius in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, whereas a constriction comparison is naturally diameter-like (maximum molecular cross-section, for which GeDi is the analogous pair-distance quantity). Pairing a COM radius against the free-sphere diameter lsd_f mixes radius and diameter conventions, and hydrogen exclusion (native representation) systematically underestimates the full van der Waals extent that controls passage. The descriptor remains computable, but the geometric comparison is approximate and the mapping is an empirical choice, not an established equivalence.

SPAN = 0 for 54 single-site training rows (legitimate physical zeros) pins the descriptor at exactly 1 for those rows, independent of lsd_f: the descriptor carries no framework-confinement signal there. The draft's claim that descriptor = 1 is 'physically interpretable as no geometric confinement for a point-like adsorbate' is an interpretive assertion, not an established fact; single-site adsorbates can still lose translational/rotational entropy on adsorption, and the training notes state that positive reference medians do not remove input zeros. The derivative check (nonzero_fraction ~0.977, consistent with 54/2361 zero-derivative rows) confirms this dead zone but does not validate the interpretation.

Partial mechanism transfer: E03 reports that adsorption entropy losses arise from BOTH translational and rotational motions, and E06 additionally proposes rotational freedom as possibly substantial for adsorption equilibrium. The draft isolates only the translational channel and explicitly makes no rotational claim. This restriction is an assumption not established by the cited sources; the retained rotational contribution is not represented anywhere in the descriptor.

No source in the preserved evidence supports bottleneck-controlled (as opposed to cavity-controlled) translational confinement; the hypothesis that the narrowest accessible passage governs retained translational freedom is a source-external construction. execution_check.mechanism_validated is false and scientific_consistency is 'structural_checks_passed_semantics_unverified', so the structural and limit checks do not corroborate the mechanism. Knowledge-graph edges from cavity_rotation/mfi_fau_rotation to SPAN are absent; per the task constraint, this absence is unknown rather than disproof, but it means the SPAN proxy link rests solely on the draft's own assumption.

Directional physical prediction is untestable with the provided record: no target values are given, the target is defined as (Sgas - Sads)/R while the ANN predicts Sads/Sgas (loss is NOT -log(Sads/Sgas)), and the derivative check only verifies descriptor monotonicity in lsd_f (regime_input is lsd_f itself, i.e., the descriptor is checked against its own input, not against any outcome). The claim that entropy loss decreases with increasing lsd_f at fixed SPAN remains an unverified hypothesis.

The draft's own stated competing explanation — that the descriptor may correlate with framework density or ASA through topology rather than encoding a translational-confinement mechanism — is unresolved in this record. There are no graph edges connecting lsd_f to density or ASA; absent edges are unknown and do not disprove the confounding pathway, but no evidence here excludes it before mechanism attribution, as the falsification criteria themselves require.

Sensitivity and functional form: the descriptor is bounded in (0, 1] with limits 1 (lsd_f -> infinity) and 0 (SPAN -> infinity); the saturating ratio form compresses differences for large pores and for small adsorbates, so the working dynamic range within training support (lsd_f up to 7.68726 angstrom, SPAN median 1.86060 angstrom) may be narrow for much of the domain. The form is an explicitly stated empirical choice with no fitted coefficients, which is honest, but neither the form nor its sensitivity is validated by any source in the record.

Normalization distinction preserved correctly but worth recording: the descriptor uses native inputs only (no q-normalization), so the q-ratio caveat (q-ratio = 1 is not native equality) does not apply; however, the descriptor value 1 at SPAN = 0 is a value on the descriptor's own arbitrary scale and must not be read as a physical equality or threshold condition.

final_candidate.name: bottleneck_to_included_sphere_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R depends on whether the framework confines the molecule mainly within bounded cages behind narrow windows versus along connected channels, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + lsd_p) is monotonically related to the loss: a small ratio means the largest included free sphere along the free path (lsd_p, Dif) greatly exceeds the passing bottleneck (lsd_f, Df), i.e. a cage-window architecture in which the molecule is spatially locked inside a bounded cavity and loses more translational freedom (and, in the tightest windows, rotational freedom); a ratio near unity means Df and Dif are comparable, i.e. an open channel-like topology in which the molecule retains at least one extended direction of mobility, hence smaller entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03), and is consistent with the MCM-22 supercage picture in which adsorption concentrates in closed cages (E06), but expressed purely through the contrast between the two Ze++ free-sphere radii rather than through either radius alone.
final_candidate.rationale: Prior rounds used lsd_p against molecular extension (GeDi) and lsd_f against molecular extension (SPAN); both couple one framework radius to one molecular size. This descriptor uses only framework geometry and captures topology (window-to-cage contrast), a dimension the two prior descriptors cannot express: two frameworks with identical Dif can differ in whether that free space is a bounded cage or a connected channel. Limitations: Df and Dif are Ze++ fixed-probe geometric radii, not measurements of lost degrees of freedom; Dif is not the global cavity diameter Di and Df is not a window aperture measured crystallographically; the descriptor says nothing about framework chemistry, loading, or temperature. descriptor_candidate.name: bottleneck_to_included_sphere_ratio
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R depends on whether the framework confines the molecule mainly within bounded cages behind narrow windows versus along connected channels, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + lsd_p) is monotonically related to the loss: a small ratio means the largest included free sphere along the free path (lsd_p, Dif) greatly exceeds the passing bottleneck (lsd_f, Df), i.e. a cage-window architecture in which the molecule is spatially locked inside a bounded cavity and loses more translational freedom (and, in the tightest windows, rotational freedom); a ratio near unity means Df and Dif are comparable, i.e. an open channel-like topology in which the molecule retains at least one extended direction of mobility, hence smaller entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03), and is consistent with the MCM-22 supercage picture in which adsorption concentrates in closed cages (E06), but expressed purely through the contrast between the two Ze++ free-sphere radii rather than through either radius alone.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: Prior rounds used lsd_p against molecular extension (GeDi) and lsd_f against molecular extension (SPAN); both couple one framework radius to one molecular size. This descriptor uses only framework geometry and captures topology (window-to-cage contrast), a dimension the two prior descriptors cannot express: two frameworks with identical Dif can differ in whether that free space is a bounded cage or a connected channel. Limitations: Df and Dif are Ze++ fixed-probe geometric radii, not measurements of lost degrees of freedom; Dif is not the global cavity diameter Di and Df is not a window aperture measured crystallographically; the descriptor says nothing about framework chemistry, loading, or temperature. The direction of the effect (cage-like = larger loss) is a hypothesized transfer of qualitative literature comparisons, not an established relation for this benchmark.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The monotone hypothesis fails if: (1) entropy loss tracks the absolute included sphere size (larger lsd_p means smaller loss) regardless of bottleneck contrast, so that large-cage/small-window frameworks show small loss contrary to prediction; (2) channel-like frameworks with lsd_f close to lsd_p show larger entropy loss than cage-like frameworks at comparable lsd_p (e.g. because narrow channels restrict rotation more than large cages do, as in the E01/E02 MFI-vs-FAU rotational comparison); or (3) the contrast carries no information beyond what lsd_f or lsd_p alone provide in this dataset. If any of these hold, the descriptor direction is wrong or redundant.
descriptor_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the Df/Dif contrast distinguishes cage-window from channel-like accessibility for the adsorbate-relevant free path; assumes smaller contrast (cage-like topology) implies greater translational confinement and entropy loss, by analogy to reported cage-vs-channel entropy comparisons (E02, E04, E06); assumes Ze++ fixed-probe free-sphere radii are adequate geometric proxies for these regimes. These are proxy assumptions and literature-conditional transfers, not demonstrated causality for this benchmark.

prior_formulas.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how tightly a molecule geometrically fits inside the framework's largest accessible free-space region, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest included free sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) is large relative to the molecule's maximum heavy-atom extension (GeDi) permit more retained rotational and translational freedom, hence smaller entropy loss; frameworks where the molecule nearly fills the free space force greater entropy loss. This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-size vs rotational-entropy-loss comparison (E02, C2) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03, C3) into a molecule-framework coupling descriptor.

If the translational component of adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how much a molecule's spatial extent is confined by the framework's narrowest accessible passage, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest passing free sphere (lsd_f, the Df bottleneck) is large relative to the molecule's heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) permit more retained translational freedom and hence smaller entropy loss, while frameworks whose bottleneck barely admits the molecule force greater translational entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03) into a bottleneck-side molecule-framework coupling descriptor, complementary to the round-1 included-sphere descriptor lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi).

However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. review_issues.explanation: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df, passing bottleneck) and lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif, included sphere along the free-sphere path) are distinct quantities per the diameter_roles constraint. Interpreting their ratio as a cage-vs-channel topology indicator is a proxy assumption: Df is not a crystallographic window aperture and Dif is not the global cavity diameter Di, so the ratio is not itself a physically defined topology measurement. The sum lsd_f + lsd_p in the denominator adds a passing radius to an included radius that measure different geometric features and does not correspond to any native length scale.

The claim that the descriptor lies in (0,1) relies on per-sample lsd_p >= lsd_f (included sphere along the free-sphere path must be at least the passing sphere). The provided training statistics are marginal quantiles over 2361 rows and do not verify this ordering row-wise. The quoted descriptor range [0.052, 0.697] is also derived from marginal extremes; extrema of a ratio need not occur at independent marginal endpoints, so the stated range is an approximation, not a verified bound.

The conditional prediction varies lsd_f while holding lsd_p fixed. Because the free-sphere path definition implies the included sphere along that path is at least the passing sphere (Dif >= Df), arbitrarily raising lsd_f against a fixed lsd_p can produce configurations where the passing sphere exceeds the included sphere along the path, which is definitionally unrealizable. The predicted monotone direction is therefore only meaningful in the subset of input combinations consistent with the Df/Dif ordering; this restriction is not stated in the prediction.

The descriptor is purely framework-side and adsorbate-independent, while the target entropy loss depends on both molecule and framework (training spans 2361 molecule-framework pairs; adsorbate geometry proxies MW/LabuteASA/PBF/PMI/SPAN/GeDi/Vol are unused). The hypothesis asserts greater translational and rotational confinement in cage-like frameworks, but rotational confinement intrinsically depends on molecular size relative to the cavity (as in E01/E02 and the radius-of-gyration comparison in E06). A monotone framework-only relation can at best hold conditional on adsorbate; no rotor_case or molecule-size conditioning is expressed.

The ratio conflates absolute included free-space size with topology contrast. A framework with a large bottleneck and an even larger cage can share the same ratio as a narrow-window/small-cage framework, yet E02 indicates absolute cavity size independently governs rotational entropy loss (larger cavity, smaller loss). The descriptor therefore cannot separate the E02 absolute-size effect from the hypothesized connectivity effect; this confounding is acknowledged in falsification criterion (1) but remains unaddressed in the hypothesis itself.

E02 reports the FER/FAU rotational-entropy comparison using average cavity diameter (FER ~ 4.3 A, FAU ~ 13 A), which is the global cavity diameter Di. Neither lsd_f (Df, passing bottleneck) nor lsd_p (Dif, included along the free path) is Di; transferring the reported comparison to a Df/Dif ratio requires an explicit mapping that is listed as an open transfer assumption (C2) and is not demonstrated. The mechanism card records a reported comparison for a different geometric quantity, and mechanism_validated is false.

E06 is MCM-22-specific: adsorption is inferred to concentrate in supercages, and the cited diffusion statements concern 450-850 K; the relation is recorded as SOURCE_PROPOSES_POSSIBLE_EFFECT (cage_rotational_equilibrium) with conditional status. Using E06 to support a general cage-window-vs-channel entropy-loss direction for all frameworks in this benchmark is a literature-conditional transfer, not an established relation; temperature, loading, and framework chemistry remain unresolved in the excerpts (C1-C4, C6).

Falsification criterion (2) and the proxy_assumptions field invoke the MFI-vs-FAU rotational-entropy comparisons (E01, E04), but the draft's evidence_ids list only contains E02, E03, E06. The cited support for the rotational component of the hypothesis is therefore incompletely recorded in the evidence list. Separately, the direction of the effect (cage-like = larger loss) is hypothesized, not validated; unknown or absent graph support elsewhere cannot be treated as disproof, and the internal derivative check (nonzero_fraction 1.0, opposite_n 0) only verifies monotonicity of the expression, not the mechanism.

draft_candidate.name: bottleneck_to_included_sphere_ratio
draft_candidate.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R depends on whether the framework confines the molecule mainly within bounded cages behind narrow windows versus along connected channels, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + lsd_p) is monotonically related to the loss: a small ratio means the largest included free sphere along the free path (lsd_p, Dif) greatly exceeds the passing bottleneck (lsd_f, Df), i.e. a cage-window architecture in which the molecule is spatially locked inside a bounded cavity and loses more translational freedom (and, in the tightest windows, rotational freedom); a ratio near unity means Df and Dif are comparable, i.e. an open channel-like topology in which the molecule retains at least one extended direction of mobility, hence smaller entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03), and is consistent with the MCM-22 supercage picture in which adsorption concentrates in closed cages (E06), but expressed purely through the contrast between the two Ze++ free-sphere radii rather than through either radius alone.
draft_candidate.rationale: Prior rounds used lsd_p against molecular extension (GeDi) and lsd_f against molecular extension (SPAN); both couple one framework radius to one molecular size. This descriptor uses only framework geometry and captures topology (window-to-cage contrast), a dimension the two prior descriptors cannot express: two frameworks with identical Dif can differ in whether that free space is a bounded cage or a connected channel. Limitations: Df and Dif are Ze++ fixed-probe geometric radii, not measurements of lost degrees of freedom; Dif is not the global cavity diameter Di and Df is not a window aperture measured crystallographically; the descriptor says nothing about framework chemistry, loading, or temperature. The direction of the effect (cage-like = larger loss) is a hypothesized transfer of qualitative literature comparisons, not an established relation for this benchmark.
draft_candidate.falsification_criteria: The monotone hypothesis fails if: (1) entropy loss tracks the absolute included sphere size (larger lsd_p means smaller loss) regardless of bottleneck contrast, so that large-cage/small-window frameworks show small loss contrary to prediction; (2) channel-like frameworks with lsd_f close to lsd_p show larger entropy loss than cage-like frameworks at comparable lsd_p (e.g. because narrow channels restrict rotation more than large cages do, as in the E01/E02 MFI-vs-FAU rotational comparison); or (3) the contrast carries no information beyond what lsd_f or lsd_p alone provide in this dataset. If any of these hold, the descriptor direction is wrong or redundant.
draft_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the Df/Dif contrast distinguishes cage-window from channel-like accessibility for the adsorbate-relevant free path; assumes smaller contrast (cage-like topology) implies greater translational confinement and entropy loss, by analogy to reported cage-vs-channel entropy comparisons (E02, E04, E06); assumes Ze++ fixed-probe free-sphere radii are adequate geometric proxies for these regimes. These are proxy assumptions and literature-conditional transfers, not demonstrated causality for this benchmark.

Descriptor range on training support is approximately [0.052, 0.697]. No rotor_case branch needed; no log/exp of dimensional quantities.

appended.name: pore_to_molecule_fit_ratio
appended.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how tightly a molecule geometrically fits inside the framework's largest accessible free-space region, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest included free sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) is large relative to the molecule's maximum heavy-atom extension (GeDi) permit more retained rotational and translational freedom, hence smaller entropy loss; frameworks where the molecule nearly fills the free space force greater entropy loss. This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-size vs rotational-entropy-loss comparison (E02, C2) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03, C3) into a molecule-framework coupling descriptor.
appended.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement coupling between adsorbate size and framework free space. lsd_p is used as the included-along-free-path sphere (Dif), NOT the passing bottleneck Df and NOT a global cavity diameter Di; the E02 'cavity diameter' mechanism is therefore only proxied, since Dif measures the largest sphere sitting along the free-sphere path rather than an average or global cavity size. GeDi is the largest distance between two heavy atoms in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full all-atom molecular envelope (hydrogens excluded) and is legitimately zero for the 54 single-site species; at GeDi = 0 the ratio degenerates to 1, which should be read as 'no resolvable size-based confinement penalty for this proxy', not as a physical claim of free rotation. The ratio is dimensionless, bounded in (0, 1], uses only native inputs and arithmetic, and requires no rotor_case branching because no inertia logs are taken. This is an empirical proxy construction; the source evidence reports qualitative comparisons on specific zeolite pairs (MFI/FAU, FER/FAU, MCM-22) and supplies no fitted coefficients, so no source-specific percentage is imported.
appended.falsification_criteria: The descriptor fails if (1) within the training range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) at fixed GeDi, the conditional physical entropy loss does not decrease as the ratio increases (i.e., the fit-to-confinement hypothesis has the wrong sign or no signal); or (2) a competing explanation accounts better: entropy loss driven instead by framework chemistry/adsorption energetics or by the passing bottleneck lsd_f rather than the included sphere lsd_p, in which case swapping lsd_p for lsd_f in the same ratio would outperform, indicating the Dif role assignment was wrong; or (3) the signal is carried entirely by GeDi alone (molecule-size effect) with no incremental framework-dependence, reducing the ratio to a disguised adsorbate-size descriptor.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes: (a) lsd_p (Dif) is a usable proxy for the confining free-space scale relevant to retained rotational/translational freedom, acknowledging it is neither Df nor a guaranteed global cavity diameter; (b) GeDi proxies the molecule's largest spatial extension relevant to rotating inside the pore, acknowledging hydrogens are excluded and single-site species give GeDi = 0 by definition; (c) the additive denominator (lsd_p + GeDi) is a fixed monotone normalization choice, not a physical free-volume equality; (d) the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy-loss comparisons in zeolites transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime; none of these assumptions establishes causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom, GeDi in [0, 10.9718] angstrom. The ratio is strictly positive and bounded in (0, 1] over this support; no division-by-zero occurs because lsd_p > 0 throughout training and the denominator adds a positive constant. GeDi = 0 (54 single-site species) yields ratio = 1, a legitimate boundary value of the heavy-atom proxy, not a physical claim of unrestricted rotation; these points should be checked as a separate rotor_case branch rather than median-imputed.

appended.name: bottleneck_to_molecule_span_translational_freedom_ratio
appended.hypothesis: If the translational component of adsorption entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R is governed by how much a molecule's spatial extent is confined by the framework's narrowest accessible passage, then the dimensionless ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) is monotonically related to the loss: frameworks whose largest passing free sphere (lsd_f, the Df bottleneck) is large relative to the molecule's heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) permit more retained translational freedom and hence smaller entropy loss, while frameworks whose bottleneck barely admits the molecule force greater translational entropy loss. This transfers the reported confinement-vs-entropy-loss comparison (E02) and the translational+rotational loss mechanism (E03) into a bottleneck-side molecule-framework coupling descriptor, complementary to the round-1 included-sphere descriptor lsd_p/(lsd_p + GeDi).
appended.rationale: lsd_f is the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path (a bottleneck proxy), NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the included-along-path Dif used in round 1; using it assumes that confinement experienced by an adsorbate is at least partly controlled by the narrowest constrictions connecting accessible space, which is an assumption, not an established fact. SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full van der Waals extent (hydrogens excluded) and legitimately equals zero for the 54 single-site training rows; at SPAN = 0 the descriptor equals 1, which is finite and physically interpretable as no geometric confinement for a point-like adsorbate. The descriptor is dimensionless, defined for all training support (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom, SPAN in [0, 6.24083] angstrom), and requires no logs of inertia so no rotor_case branch is needed. Mechanistically it targets the translational freedom channel named in E03; it makes no claim about rotational freedom, energetics, or framework chemistry, and it does not assert that the bottleneck equals the local adsorption environment (adsorption may occur in cavities larger than the bottleneck).
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding SPAN fixed within its training quantiles, entropy loss increases rather than decreases with increasing lsd_f, or if the empirical loss is better explained by cavity-size proxies (e.g., lsd_p-based or AV-based descriptors) with no residual dependence on the bottleneck lsd_f — which would indicate confinement is set by the adsorption site volume, not the narrowest passage. A competing explanation is that the descriptor merely correlates with framework density or ASA through framework topology rather than encoding a translational-confinement mechanism; this must be excluded before attributing the mechanism.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) lsd_f (Df bottleneck) is a usable proxy for the constriction-controlled part of translational confinement, distinct from cavity Di and from Dif; (2) SPAN (heavy-atom, implicit-H) is a usable proxy for molecular spatial extent, acknowledging hydrogen atoms are excluded; (3) a saturating ratio form lsd_f/(lsd_f + SPAN) approximates retained translational freedom, with no fitted coefficients; (4) transfer of reported MFI/FAU/FER confinement-entropy statements to the benchmark regime at unspecified temperature and loading is hypothetical. No causal or novel mechanism is claimed; the descriptor is a testable geometric coupling proxy.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: lsd_f is strictly positive (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the denominator never vanishes; SPAN = 0 for 54 single-site training rows is a legitimate physical zero preserved by the expression (descriptor = 1, no division by SPAN), not imputed or excluded; descriptor range is (0, 1] and monotone decreasing in SPAN and increasing in lsd_f.
